kind_note: research prototype: an orchestration framework that discovers agent harnesses, described in an arXiv paper
note: Corrections: lab 'unknown' is still unresolved, since I did not open the paper's author affiliations. Kind 'harness' is off: MILO is a search and orchestration system that co-evolves agent harnesses and the strategy used to discover them, not a harness shipped to users. Source: 'MILO: Automated Harness Discovery via Orchestrated Multi-Agent Evolution' (arXiv 2609.38349; Hugging Face paper page https://huggingface.co/papers/2609.38349). I found no code repository, product, or launch announcement, and no public-availability statement. Reported results (Terminal-Bench 2.1, 86.1 ± 2.0%) come from the abstract and third-party summaries, not a released artifact. No date is sourced for the paper itself: the arXiv ID suggests a 2026 submission, and a lilys.ai digest URL is dated 2026-10-01, but neither is a release date. Unrelated 'MILO' products found and excluded: Miloverse's MILO (ALPHA) kids' creative AI app, FAAC's MILO VR training simulator, the miloteam Docker image, and the miloR R package.
